reference.source: Eastman N. Jacobs and Kenneth E. Ward, Interference of Wing and Fuselage from Tests of 209 Combinations in the N.A.C.A. Variable-Density Tunnel, NACA Report No. 540, 1936 (Langley, 8 March 1935). Table V, combination 15, rectangular NACA 0012 with the round fuselage, wing setting i_w = 0. The column n_0 is dC_m/dC_L at zero lift, the aerodynamic centre as a fraction of the wing chord ahead of the wing quarter-chord (report p. 8). xbar_np = 0.25 - n_0, from the leading edge of the MAC.
reference.conditions: Variable-density tunnel, Reynolds number about 3.1e6 (report p. 4). Mach is not stated; the tunnel is low-speed, so the AVL run uses Mach 0. Moments about the wing quarter-chord; coefficients on the original wing area and chord (150 in^2, c = 5 in, b = 30 in, AR = 6). d/c positive is the wing quarter-chord ahead of the fuselage reference; k/c positive is the wing chord plane above the fuselage axis (report p. 8). The fuselage reference is the maximum cross-section: station 8.000 in on p. 3, 8.156 in aft of the nose (station -0.156 in), because Figure 1 draws that point through the maximum ordinate. Stations 1.500, 2.312 and 3.406 in are omitted: 1.500 is blank in the printed diameter column and 2.312 / 3.406 are the dashed source-sink rows, not diameters. Model scale is the tunnel model (inches converted at 0.0254 m/in). The wing is the rectangular NACA 0012, no twist, no dihedral. This row: combination 15, d/c = 0.0, k/c = 0.16, i_w = 0 deg, n_0 = 0.034 (Table V).
